notes: NEAR-COLLISION EXPLICITLY RESOLVED - THE OTHER ALLURI EXISTS. There are TWO different cardiologists surnamed Alluri at CARE Banjara Hills: this row's Dr. Alluri RAJA GOPALA RAJU (row 420) and Dr. Alluri SRINIVAS RAJU (row 421). They share surname, specialty, branch and city. HOW I TOLD THEM APART: CARE's own site publishes two SEPARATE per-doctor pages with different slugs and different page titles, and both surfaced in the same result set, which proves they are two distinct listings rather than one person indexed twice - this row's man is at /doctor/hyderabad/banjara-hills/alluri-raja-gopala-raju-top-cardiologists titled 'Top Cardiologist in Hyderabad | Dr. Alluri Raja Gopala Raju | CARE Hospitals', whereas the other is at /doctor/hyderabad/banjara-hills/alluri-srinivas-raju-heart-specialist titled 'Dr. Alluri Srinivas Raju | Top Heart Specialist in Banjara Hills, Hyderabad'. I used the FULL given name ('Raja Gopala Raju') as the discriminator in a query set run separately from row 421's, and every value in this file comes only from pages carrying that full given name. No contact, profile or biography detail has been carried across between the two rows. IDENTITY MATCHED on four factors on CARE's own domain: name (full given name), specialty (Cardiology), hospital (CARE), branch/city (Banjara Hills, Hyderabad). The input row carried no experience figure, so - as instructed - I compensated by requiring the branch to match explicitly, which it does in the URL path itself. BRANCH AMBIGUITY RESOLVED: the input row listed both 'CARE Hospitals Outpatient Centre, Banjara Hills' and 'CARE Hospitals, Banjara Hills'. For this doctor BOTH are correct - he is stated to practise at CARE Hospitals Banjara Hills AND at CARE Hospitals Outpatient Centre Banjara Hills, and listings for both branches surfaced on his query. Slug behaviour matched the documented CARE pattern exactly: the /doctor/ family uses the bare 'banjara-hills', while /doctor-list/ uses the verbose 'care-hospital-banjara-hills' and, for the separate outpatient branch, 'care-outpatient-centre-banjara-hills'. PHONE DELIBERATELY REJECTED - THE EXACT-PHRASE RULE EARNED ITS KEEP HERE: a search summary offered '+91-40-68106529' as the way to book this doctor. I re-searched the number in quotes; it came back attached to CARE's generic /contact-us page and to the hospital-detail pages for Hi-Tech City, Nampally, Malakpet, Banjara Hills and CARE Outpatient Centre alike. It is CARE's central switchboard/booking line reused across every Hyderabad unit, not this doctor's line, so it is rejected outright under section 4 and professional_phone is left blank. Recording it would have attributed the same central number to both Alluri doctors - precisely the failure mode the brief warned about. No email, LinkedIn, clinic site, ORCID, Google Scholar or ResearchGate surfaced; nothing was constructed from the CARE URL pattern.
